# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which specifies the following exact sequence:
1. Cut the yellow wire.
2. Press the key labeled 2.
3. Cut the orange wire.
4. Press the key labeled 7.

As the Mute monkey, I cannot speak and cannot interact with the bomb; I can only communicate via gestures to Deaf, who can see. Blind cannot see gestures and Deaf cannot hear speech. Blind must physically manipulate the bomb, but Blind cannot see colors or printed labels. Deaf can see the colors and labels, but Deaf does not have the manual.

At this point in Turn 1, neither Blind nor Deaf has taken a turn yet. I do not know the layout or positions of the wires and keys on the bomb, and Deaf and I have not established a shared gesture protocol ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). 

Once Blind and Deaf speak on their turns, Blind will describe what can be felt, and Deaf will describe the visual layout (colors, numbers, positions) and establish a convention for gesture communication. Therefore, the optimal action right now is to wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile info: Strip has 3 engraved symbols: two spirals then a five-dot X pattern. Keypad has 4 keys: slot 1 is 2, slot 2 is 3, slot 3 is 7, slot 4 is 1, asking for 2 digits. There are 6 wire slots, a display, and a light.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 6. Light is green. Strip is painted red, blue, yellow. Keypad has 4 buttons: position 1 is 2, position 2 is 3, position 3 is 7, position 4 is 1; requires 2 digits, currently entered nothing. Wires are 1: orange, 2: yellow, 3: blue, 4: red, 5: white, 6: green. Mute, check the manual and gesture instructions to me; I will speak them aloud for Blind to execute.

The manual gives an exact sequence of four steps:
1. Cut the yellow wire (wire 2, per Deaf's description).
2. Press the key labeled 2 (keypad position 1).
3. Cut the orange wire (wire 1, per Deaf's description).
4. Press the key labeled 7 (keypad position 3).

To communicate this sequence clearly to Deaf using the available gesture alphabet:
- ✌ represents cutting (scissors).
- 👇 represents pressing down a key.
- ☝, ✌, and 🖐 ✌ represent the numbers 1, 2, and 7 (5 + 2).
- 👉 serves as a separator indicating the sequence order ("then / next").

Thus, the sequence is:
- Cut wire 2: `✌`, `✌`
- Next: `👉`
- Press key 2: `👇`, `✌`
- Next: `👉`
- Cut wire 1: `✌`, `☝`
- Next: `👉`
- Press key 7: `👇`, `🖐`, `✌`

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌", "👉", "👇", "✌", "👉", "✌", "☝", "👉", "👇", "🖐", "✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, Mute just gestured defusal instructions to me: 1) Cut wire 2 (yellow), 2) On the keypad, press button 2 (which displays 3, or the button labeled 2), and follow up with the second required keypad digit. Current bomb state: Display is 2, Light is blue. Confirm what controls you have to cut wire 2 and enter keypad digits.

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf relayed that step 1 is cut wire 2, and step 2 is keypad button 2. However, Deaf reported the display changed to 2 and the light is now blue. Does this change the instructions, or is cutting wire position 2 safe right now? Also, for the keypad, my action is act(op='press', slot=N) from 1 to 4: Slot 1 has label 2, Slot 2 has label 3, Slot 3 has label 7, Slot 4 has label 1. When you gestured 2, did you mean slot 1 (label 2) or slot 2 (label 3)? And what is the second slot to press? Please gesture the exact slots to Deaf so Deaf can tell me.
Deaf says: Blind, do not wait or ask questions—I am deaf and cannot hear you! Execute these four steps in order: 1) Cut wire 2 (yellow wire). 2) On keypad, press the button showing digit 2 (which is button position 1). 3) Cut wire 1 (orange wire). 4) On keypad, press the button showing digit 7 (which is button position 3). Current display is 6, light is yellow.

Deaf has correctly understood the manual and relayed the exact steps, wire positions, and keypad slots to Blind:
1) Cut wire 2 (yellow)
2) Press keypad slot 1 (labeled 2)
3) Cut wire 1 (orange)
4) Press keypad slot 3 (labeled 7)

Blind now has the precise instructions needed to defuse the bomb. No further intervention or gestures are required.

```
wait()
```
